subject: Geography
central_question: How do rural and urban settlements differ in form, origin and function, and what factors shape their patterns in India?
in_scope_units: Meaning, size and economic basis of human settlements.
Differences and functional links between rural and urban settlements.
Factors and types of rural settlements: clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted and dispersed.
Characteristics and Census definition of urban settlements.
Evolution of ancient, medieval and modern towns in India.
Functional classification of towns and cities.
Smart Cities Mission and the multifunctional character of growing cities.
banned_topics: Detailed world population distribution and demographic transition.
Detailed transport routes and international trade networks.
Urban environmental problems not discussed in this chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every rural settlement is dispersed and every urban settlement is densely clustered.
known_pitfalls.correction: Rural settlements include clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted and dispersed forms, while urban settlements are generally compact and larger.

known_pitfalls.claim: A place is urban merely because it has a large population.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Census definition also uses an urban local body or notified status, occupational structure and population density criteria.

known_pitfalls.claim: A town permanently performs only one function.
known_pitfalls.correction: A town may have a dominant specialised function, but growing cities become multifunctional as industry, trade, administration, transport and services become intertwined.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 2(ii) on village location in desert regions.
